name: @aztec-avm-runtime/replay
description: L0 of the live-chain replay campaign: a node client narrowed to what a replay needs
//: WHY THIS TREE IS ON `npm.current` AND orchestration/ IS NOT. pins.json declares two @aztec
nightly lines on purpose. `deletion_era` (5.0.0-nightly.20260626) is FROZEN EVIDENCE: the
published line whose src/public tree is byte-comparable with the `ts` anchor, which is what
lets the deleted TypeScript AVM run at all. It has nothing to say about which protocol a
RUNNING chain speaks. `current` (5.3.0-nightly.20260819) declares
`corresponds_to_anchor: cpp`, and the cpp anchor is the one every L0 enumeration is
re-derived from, so it is the line a client that talks to a live node belongs on.
CONSEQUENCE, STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED: this package and orchestration/ have DIFFERENT
@aztec/stdlib installs, and importing across the boundary is a wrong answer rather than an
inefficiency — `serializeWithMessagePack` recognises an `Fr` by the class object of its own
install, which lib_m21_form_b.sh already records. That is the stated rejection reason for
not importing orchestration/src/settled_read_source.ts's `strictSurface`; replay/src has its
own, citing M21's design decision by decision.
@aztec/noir-protocol-circuits-types IS A devDependency AND MUST STAY ONE. It is 92 MB and it
is needed by exactly one thing: verify_client_uses_upstream_schema, which re-derives
live_chain.protocol_version.l2CircuitsVkTreeRoot from `getVKTreeRoot()` so that the pin is a
measurement rather than a transcription. Nothing the client ships imports it, and DD-9's
browser boundary is the reason that matters at L4.
@aztec/protocol-contracts is a runtime dependency of nothing here either, and is declared for
the same re-derivation (`protocolContractsHash`). It is 2.6 MB and L1 will need it for real,
so it is a plain dependency rather than a dev one.
NO @aztec/aztec.js AND NO @aztec/pxe. A PXE is the private half's home and a replayed
transaction has no private half; aztec.js would bring a wallet, a key store and a note
database for a client that only reads. The one thing this package needs from that direction —
`createAztecNodeClient` — is in @aztec/stdlib/interfaces/client, which is already here.
